finding.summary: Shrinking the used bounds (clearing the last populated cell) leaves formulas over unbounded ranges stale
finding.evidence: `buildDependantsMap` computes `const bounds = this.cellIndex.bounds()` *after* the edit has been applied, then expands each formula against those bounds. When the edit deletes the cell that defined the extent (e.g. A10 cleared while `=SUM(A:A)` exists), bounds have already shrunk to r<=3, so the formula's dependency set is A1:A3 and does not contain A10; the dirty cell A10 therefore has no dependants and the formula is never recalculated, keeping the pre-delete total on screen. The new test only covers the growth direction ('picks up a newly added cell beyond the prior data extent'), not deletion. Same logic in YorkieStore.buildDependantsMap.
